title: Crosswind Council
logline: At council, keys may be filed smaller, never grown in secret. No key yet covers the egg.
epigraph: Benefit without cost is rumor; cost without benefit is ruin.
description: Chapter 4 of Lore.Land: Crosswind Council. Boon and bane sit under shared weather with keys that can only be narrowed. The egg sits between them, a cell no key covers.

content.text: Council hill kept a table that did not pick a side. Boof set the egg on the wood between two keys and stumbled, almost, upon the

children.text: — a pane of weather that showed not a face but the size of a permission. One key was iron and already filed smaller. One key was brass and wanted to grow. The law of the table was older than the argument: a key may be narrowed. A key may never be grown in secret.

content.text: The Fool’s Mirror shimmered with the shared storm. It whispered, "What you see is not what is, but what you are still allowed to do." Boon saw a harvest. Bane saw a constraint. The egg saw neither. It kept its own law, which is what a cell does when no key covers it.
"Look into the glass, Boof," the Fool’s voice carried on the crosswind. "In it you will see not me, but the edge of your key. File it smaller if you must. Do not pretend it grew overnight."

img.alt: A council table under storm-light, two keys and a coal-dark cracked egg the keys cannot cover.

sections.figcaption: Crosswind Council: keys narrow; they do not secretly widen.

sections.title: The Reflections of the Fool’s Mirror

content.text: As Boof gazed into the glass, her reflection shifted with the weather. Boon and bane sat under one roof and bargained without declaring war. The membrane between them was the table itself — you could share a turn across it without giving the house away. No key on the wood fitted the egg. Filing them smaller only made the uncovered cell more obvious.

content.text: Boof left both keys on the table. A key you do not take cannot be accused of growing. She took the egg. Downslope the counting rooms had begun to disagree with themselves — two receipts that could not both post. That was a rift, not a vote.

loreItems.description: A key may be filed smaller, never grown in secret. That is the council's oldest weather.
The egg is a cell: it keeps its own law. No key on the table covers it.
Sharing across a membrane is not giving the house away. Boon and bane can sit one turn without becoming one office.
